findings.highlight: I've been distancing myself from Takeya, who's been calling me every single day. And every time I hang up, the feeling of guilt envelops me, eating me alive.
findings.evidenceJa: 『あの日』以降、毎日連絡をくれる武也に対して、あしらい気味に扱ってしまいつつ、電話を切ってから詫びるの繰り返し。
findings.explanation: Haruki describes a repeated concrete routine: he brushes off Takeya, who calls daily, then apologizes after ending the call. The translation replaces the apology with invented, highly intensified guilt that 'envelops' and 'eats [him] alive,' turning observed conduct into purple psychological narration.
findings.japanese:
『あの日』以降、毎日連絡をくれる武也に対して、
あしらい気味に扱ってしまいつつ、
電話を切ってから詫びるの繰り返し。
findings.todokanai: Ever since "that day," I've been distancing myself from Takeya, who's been calling me every single day. And every time I hang up, the feeling of guilt envelops me, eating me alive.

findings.highlight: cruel feelings that value nothing of their friendship
findings.evidenceJa: 友達甲斐のない残酷な気持ちだった
findings.explanation: Haruki calls his desire to be left alone cruel and 友達甲斐のない: unworthy of a friend or showing himself to be a poor friend. The translation instead says his feelings place no value on the friendship, changing a self-accusation about what he gives his friends into a denial that he values them.
findings.japanese:
それが俺の、正直で率直で、
そして、友達甲斐のない残酷な気持ちだった。
findings.todokanai: These are nothing but my frank, direct and cruel feelings that value nothing of their friendship.

findings.highlight: the reason they were so on point with their suspicions was because they already knew the answer to begin with
findings.evidenceJa: きっと、わかっているからこそ的を射た
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks that precisely because Io and Takeya understand him and Setsuna so well, whatever they say now will hit the mark. The translation invents prior suspicions and an answer they already know, severing the line from the following prediction that they will force the pair toward a solution.
findings.japanese: きっと、わかっているからこそ的を射た…
findings.todokanai: Chances are, the reason they were so on point with their suspicions was because they already knew the answer to begin with…

findings.highlight: That's exactly why I can't betray their trust. I have to do my utmost to ensure that everything is done on time, carefully, and accurately…
findings.evidenceJa:
だからこそ、その信用を裏切る訳にはいかない。
どの仕事も納期通り、質を下げず、量を削らず、
丁寧に、そして確実にこなしていかないと…
findings.explanation: Haruki explicitly vows to meet every deadline without lowering quality or cutting quantity; 'on time, carefully, and accurately' omits the no-compromise pair.
findings.japanese:
だからこそ、その信用を裏切る訳にはいかない。
どの仕事も納期通り、質を下げず、量を削らず、
丁寧に、そして確実にこなしていかないと…
findings.todokanai: That's exactly why I can't betray their trust. I have to do my utmost to ensure that everything is done on time, carefully, and accurately…

findings.highlight: If I recall correctly, printed on that piece of paper is the name "Touma Youko."
findings.evidenceJa: 正確には、その紙面に印刷された『冬馬曜子』の文字が。
findings.explanation: 正確には means 'more precisely': Haruki corrects the preceding sentence to say it is specifically the printed name, not the sheet itself, that catches his eye. 'If I recall correctly' invents uncertainty about what the paper says and removes the deliberate self-correction.
findings.japanese:
正確には、その紙面に印刷された
『冬馬曜子』の文字が。
findings.todokanai: If I recall correctly, printed on that piece of paper is the name "Touma Youko."

findings.highlight: No, what I'd be seeing again are memories pertaining to a certain someone.
findings.evidenceJa: いや、これから集めるであろう“あいつ”のことを。
findings.explanation: The surrounding sentence says Youko's performance would make Haruki remember Kazusa, who inherited her blood and talent. Here he corrects himself: Kazusa is not already commanding audiences abroad but is the one who will do so in the future. The translation instead has him 'seeing ... memories,' eliminating both the career-time correction and the syntax of remembering her.
findings.japanese: いや、これから集めるであろう“あいつ”のことを。
findings.todokanai: No, what I'd be seeing again are memories pertaining to a certain someone.

findings.highlight: Having betrayed Setsuna, I have no business getting involved with anything pertaining to the surname of "Touma."
findings.evidenceJa:
雪菜を裏切ったまま、
“冬馬”という姓を引きずるのは。
findings.explanation: Haruki tells himself to stop dragging the Touma name along while continuing to betray Setsuna; 'no business getting involved with anything pertaining to the surname' makes it a question of external involvement rather than his own attachment.
findings.japanese:
雪菜を裏切ったまま、
“冬馬”という姓を引きずるのは。
findings.todokanai: Having betrayed Setsuna, I have no business getting involved with anything pertaining to the surname of "Touma."

findings.highlight: To the person who'd support me even if I didn't want it.
findings.evidenceJa: 嫌だと言っても支えられようとする人に。
findings.explanation: The paired morphology is deliberate: one person tries to support Haruki without being asked, while another tries to be supported by him even if he says no. The translation makes both people support Haruki, erasing the reversed dependency in the second relationship.
findings.japanese:
頼んでもいないのに支えようとする人に。
嫌だと言っても支えられようとする人に。
findings.todokanai: To the person who's supported me without me asking for it. To the person who'd support me even if I didn't want it.

findings.highlight: "Happy New Year Birthday, Mari～ Another year older."
findings.evidenceJa:
「あけましてお誕生日おめでと～麻理。
また一つ年取ったねぇ」
findings.explanation: Sawako says both Happy New Year and happy birthday because Mari's birthday is January 1; 'Happy New Year Birthday' is malformed English.
findings.japanese:
「あけましてお誕生日おめでと～麻理。
また一つ年取ったねぇ」
findings.todokanai: "Happy New Year Birthday, Mari～ Another year older."

findings.highlight: "What is…? I feel so annoyed and I can't take it anymore…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「どこがよ…
こんなモヤモヤした気持ち、たまんないわよ…」
findings.explanation: もやもや is unresolved, restless uncertainty, while 'annoyed' makes Mari's emotion primarily irritation.
findings.japanese:
「どこがよ…
こんなモヤモヤした気持ち、たまんないわよ…」
findings.todokanai: "What is…? I feel so annoyed and I can't take it anymore…"

findings.highlight: I asked Hamada-san and Suzuki-san for a way to contact the particular venue Mari-san was staying at to make sure she and her partner were safe.
findings.evidenceJa: 浜田さんか鈴木さんに頼んで、麻理さんの滞在先に連絡してもらい、彼女たちの安否を確かめてもらうために。
findings.explanation: This is the purpose for which Haruki changed clothes and rushed to the office: to ask either Hamada or Suzuki to contact Mari's lodging and confirm the women's safety. The translation says he already asked both of them for a way to contact a 'venue,' collapsing intention into completed action and mistranslating the lodging.
findings.japanese:
浜田さんか鈴木さんに頼んで、
麻理さんの滞在先に連絡してもらい、
彼女たちの安否を確かめてもらうために。
findings.todokanai: I asked Hamada-san and Suzuki-san for a way to contact the particular venue Mari-san was staying at to make sure she and her partner were safe.

findings.highlight: nearly 100% of the worst case scenarios that I had pictured were from my absurd fear
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の描いた最悪の状況なんて、ほぼ１００％杞憂で間違いないってわかってた。
findings.explanation: Haruki knew it was virtually certain that the single worst-case scenario he had imagined was a groundless fear. The translation applies 'nearly 100%' to a plurality of scenarios and says that percentage came from fear, garbling the confidence judgment that explains why he feels foolish.
findings.japanese:
俺の描いた最悪の状況なんて、
ほぼ１００％杞憂で間違いないってわかってた。
findings.todokanai: I knew full well that nearly 100% of the worst case scenarios that I had pictured were from my absurd fear.

findings.highlight: You're going to be up to your neck in more than just work if you're not careful.
findings.evidenceJa: いい加減にしないと抜けるよ色々？
findings.explanation: Suzuki warns that if Haruki keeps this up, various things will start falling out or coming loose—an ominously comic bodily consequence of overwork, to which he says 'spare me.' The translation substitutes being 'up to your neck' in unspecified things, an unrelated idiom that makes the reply and joke incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「…年越しの朝まで仕事してて、
この上まだ新しい仕事を探しますか君は。
いい加減にしないと抜けるよ色々？」
findings.todokanai: "…You worked until morning on New Year's and you're still looking for more? You're going to be up to your neck in more than just work if you're not careful."

findings.highlight: Just breaking the rules a little shouldn't be so unforgivable, right?
findings.evidenceJa: 物にあたるくらいなら、許して欲しい。
findings.explanation: After insisting that suicidal thoughts are forbidden, Haruki asks to be forgiven at least for taking his anger out on objects. The translation changes this impending physical displacement into 'breaking the rules,' obscuring both the contrast and what he is about to do.
findings.japanese:
物にあたるくらいなら、
許して欲しい。
findings.todokanai: Just breaking the rules a little shouldn't be so unforgivable, right?
